question: Does the 2018 Zambales tuna assessment add newer source-traceable fishery evidence, and can its taxa or catches be assigned to exact municipalities and capture waters or treated as independent evidence from the 1998-2002 NSAP report?

method.summary: Reviewed the official NFRDI Knowledge Products Repository metadata page and complete repository PDF through browser text extraction, including the methods, Tables 1-4, catch-composition figures, seasonality and size-composition sections, Appendix, and references. No local PDF, chart image, landing records, coordinates, or voucher data were retained.
method.studyDesign: The paper describes trained NSAP enumerators collecting catch, fishing gear, species composition and tuna length measurements from six monitored landing sites during 2003-2012. The authors say catch was raised to the number of boats landed for each day and tabulated monthly by species and gear; CPUE used raised catch data.
method.reportedCoverage: Marine tuna landings in Zambales province, with six monitored stations in Subic, Masinloc and Sta. Cruz. The article says ten of eleven coastal municipalities have tuna unloadings, but does not provide a species-by-municipality matrix. It also attributes an increase in catch partly to landings from vessels from nearby provinces.
method.reuseFinding: The PDF is available through the official NFRDI repository. No item-specific open license or reuse permission was identified in the reviewed PDF or repository metadata. Public availability is not a reuse grant; no table, chart, or app publication is approved.
method.lineageFinding: The 2003-2012 period follows the 1998-2002 Northern Zambales BFAR/NFRDI NSAP report without calendar overlap. Both are NSAP landing assessments and name overlapping municipalities/stations. Their relationship as monitoring outputs is clear, but row-level data lineage and comparability are not established; do not sum catch figures or count them as duplicate-independent evidence without the underlying records.

publication.title: Status of Tuna Resources in the Zambales Coast
publication.citation: Yutuc, R. V., Vallejo, J. Y., & Mendoza, R. A. (2018). Status of Tuna Resources in the Zambales Coast. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 25(1), 25-33. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/25.1.2017C0004
sourceLocators: Repository metadata: journal, volume 25 issue 1, 2018, and pages 25-33.
PDF printed pages 25-26: 2003-2012 study period, six monitored sites, enumeration method and raised catch.
PDF printed pages 27-31: catch totals, gear composition, seasonal distribution and size-composition claims.
PDF printed page 33: appendix naming eight tuna species.
publication.metadataNote: The PDF running header includes a Volume 24 (1-2) label on some pages, while the official repository metadata and article pagination identify Volume 25, Issue 1, pages 25-33. Use the repository record and DOI for citation.

sampling.samplingFrequencyAsReported: Every other two days, including Saturdays, Sundays and holidays; preserve the original wording because its interval is imprecise.
sampling.captureLocalityResolution: Landing-station/gear aggregates are reported. The paper says catches from fishing vessels from nearby provinces were unloaded at Zambales stations; exact catch coordinates and species-by-municipality locations are not provided.

reportedSpecies.taxonomicTreatment: The eight Appendix names are transcribed as printed. No current accepted-name crosswalk, specimen audit, or voucher review was completed; do not infer capture sites from these names.

reportedCatchContext.metricNote: Published as total landed tuna production, using raised landing data; not an individual count or biomass survey of the ecosystem.
reportedCatchContext.trendCaveat: The paper attributes increased catch partly to adding two Sta. Cruz landing centers as sampling stations and unloading by fishing vessels from nearby provinces.

reuse.licenseFinding: No item-specific open license or reuse permission identified in the reviewed PDF or repository record.

internalConsistency.issue: The abstract says eight tuna species were caught, while some result sections describe seven species for a particular gear or for size-composition analysis. The Appendix lists eight names overall.
internalConsistency.disposition: Use the eight Appendix names as the article-level roster; keep gear-specific counts separate and do not claim the list is an occurrence checklist.

internalConsistency.issue: The paper’s raised Zambales landing totals include catches unloaded at monitored ports, and the article says nearby-province vessels contributed to the increase.
internalConsistency.disposition: Treat the taxa and tonnage as source-reported landing evidence associated with the monitoring area; do not assign every fish to Zambales capture waters.

internalConsistency.issue: The 2009 stock assessment covers 1998-2002 and the 2018 tuna paper covers 2003-2012, but they share the NSAP program and some named stations; site composition and raised-data procedures may differ.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep the sources linked and their time periods separate. Do not add their totals or treat repeated taxa as independent confirmation of present-day presence.

interpretation: This is a primary historical fisheries source for eight tuna names recorded in Zambales landing records during 2003-2012.
It supplies regional and landing-station fishery context, not precise capture coordinates, a current distribution inventory, or fishing access, safety or legal advice.

It is complementary to, and temporally subsequent to, the 1998-2002 Northern Zambales NSAP assessment; the two should not be combined as one continuous or directly comparable time series without underlying data.
This marine tuna study adds no evidence for rivers, lakes, streams or wetlands.
No species assertion, occurrence row, waterbody assignment, geometry, legal or safety claim, or public-app data was added.
nextAction: Seek site-resolved catch records or a current fish survey with explicit locality, collection method, and reuse terms. Check NSAP station and source lineage before comparing or combining it with other Zambales years.
